descriptionChirho: Scripture or prophetic word is brought to completion — Arabic تَمَّ/يَتِمَّ (passive of t-m-m), Korean 이루어지다/성취되다 (be accomplished), Swahili -timizwa (be fulfilled); consistently passive voice across all target languages, indicating divine/providential agency rather than human action.

A human agent actively completes, fulfills, or accomplishes a duty, law, word, or mission — Arabic أَتَمَّ/أَكمَلَ (active causative forms of t-m-m and k-m-l), Korean 완성하다/이루다/마치다 (accomplish/complete), Swahili -timiza/-kamilisha (fulfill/complete); active voice with deliberate human agency.

A time period, course, or appointed span reaches its end — Arabic أَكمَلَ/انتَهَتْ (completed/ended), Korean 마치다 (finish), Swahili -maliza/-kamilisha (finish/complete); semantically distinct from prophecy fulfillment because the subject is a temporal duration, not a prophetic utterance.

To fill a physical space, container, or place with something — Arabic مَلَأَ/يَملأ (root m-l-ʾ, active 'to fill'), Korean 채우다 (fill), Swahili -jaza (fill); indicates physical or spatial filling with an active agent pouring, spreading, or causing something to occupy a space.

To be filled or become full, often with the Holy Spirit, joy, or other spiritual/emotional content — Arabic اِمتَلَأَ/مُمتَلِئ (Form VIII reflexive of m-l-ʾ, 'to be filled'), Korean 채워지다/충만하다 (be filled/be full), Swahili -jazwa/-jaa (be filled/become full); middle/passive voice indicating the subject as recipient of filling, frequently in spiritual contexts.
